Same for the interior '«' at 0754B ('filii et « filiae'), which is the line-start continuation mark. (4) At 0754D Migne prints NO punctuation mark between 'claruit' and 'zelus' (native crop 1000,2690,880,110): 'quia vera dixisse prophe-|tiam claruit zelus apprehendit populum ineruditum.' Our TEI is correct; the English supplies a comma and says so in the cruces.

reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both apparatus layers. Collated word by word against chunk 0004. POLARITY FINDING: at 0760C Migne prints 'sed jam idolis reprobatis, nox est laude digna' -- with est and no non -- in a gloss on the lemma '« Nec laude digna. »' (Job 3:7), so the gloss asserts the opposite of the verse it expounds. The plate carries no negative and none was supplied; the contradiction ships as printed and is logged as a crux. Also confirmed as printed and ONE WORD: 'VERS. 3. -- « Pereat dies in qua natus sum. »' at 0759C, which is the internal control for the 0748D line-break finding on f374. Further confirmed: the mixed-case italic note '(Greg. in Job l. IV.)' at 0759D, against the small-cap GREG. elsewhere; '« Est enim confusio adducens gloriam. (Eccli. IV.) »' with the period inside the guillemets; '« Caligine » Ejus noctis' with no period after the lemma; '« Non computetur in die anni. »' in the singular against the Clementine's diebus; 'Homo cum substratus, idola coluit' with cum lacking its verb.
